mechanism_fit: This realises HA (M10; tags M10, M3, M2). The entry point E is Base64Variant.encode(byte[], boolean), an existing public method that holds a self-contained field encoding: bytes to base64 text, with optional quotes and an escaped linefeed every maxLineLength/4 complete groups. A context edit reduces E's body to one statement, a delegation to the new H1 Base64Variants.encodeToText (package core). H1 keeps the former loop, quotes and linefeed counter. It composes H2 ByteArrayBuilder.packGroup (core.util), which packs 1 to 3 bytes into a big-endian 24-bit group value, and H3 CharTypes.appendBase64Group (core.io), which appends the variant's chunk or partial characters for one group. The chain spans 4 classes across 3 packages, and every helper is public static in an existing production class. The gold is H2. The fault is a quiet omission of the step its javadoc promises: each byte is to be taken as an unsigned octet and the result is to lie within 0 to 0xFFFFFF. The faulty line, bits |= data[offset + i];, is a plain compound assignment with no unusual operator. The trigger calls E directly with the UTF-8 bytes of 'cafe-acute' and fails on E's return value (Y2Fm/6k= instead of Y2Fmw6k=).
gold: com.fasterxml.jackson.core.util.ByteArrayBuilder::packGroup (src/main/java/com/fasterxml/jackson/core/util/ByteArrayBuilder.java). The fault changes `bits |= data[offset + i] & 0xFF;` to `bits |= data[offset + i];`. The minimal repair restores the mask.
decoys: com.fasterxml.jackson.core.Base64Variant::encode (Base64Variant.java, decl 'byte[] input, boolean addQuotes'): the entry point, a one-statement delegation to Base64Variants.encodeToText; its upstream javadoc is unchanged

com.fasterxml.jackson.core.Base64Variants::encodeToText (Base64Variants.java): H1, the group loop, quotes and escaped-linefeed counter. Its javadoc describes the composition (each group value from packGroup, handed to appendBase64Group)

com.fasterxml.jackson.core.io.CharTypes::appendBase64Group (CharTypes.java): H3, the non-gold helper. It forwards the group value to the upstream encodeBase64Chunk / encodeBase64Partial, and its javadoc states the precondition that bits is laid out as packGroup returns it (0 to 0xFFFFFF)
ownership_reason: ByteArrayBuilder.packGroup documents that it packs one to three bytes big-endian into the low 24 bits of an int, taking each byte as an unsigned octet (0 to 255), with bits 24 to 31 always zero, so that the result lies between 0 and 0xFFFFFF. Its loop ORs each byte into the accumulator as given (bits |= data[offset + i]), so a byte of 0x80 or more is sign-extended and sets every higher bit. For the trigger's final group (0xC3, 0xA9) it returns 0xFFFFA900 instead of 0x00C3A900, which violates both documented properties. CharTypes.appendBase64Group documents that its bits argument must be laid out as packGroup returns it (0 to 0xFFFFFF, first byte in bits 16 to 23); it only forwards the value to the unchanged upstream Base64Variant.encodeBase64Chunk / encodeBase64Partial. Given a valid group value, including values with bit 23 set, it appends the right characters, as the new passing test TestBase64Codec::testCharactersPerGroup pins. Base64Variants.encodeToText documents only that it obtains each group value from packGroup and hands it, with the byte count, to appendBase64Group, plus the quotes and the escaped-linefeed counter. The existing passing test TestBase64Generation::testStreamingWrites pins that behaviour, because it compares the output with the independent generator encoders for four variants. Base64Variant.encode is a single delegation to encodeToText. The sign extension of the second byte overwrites the first byte's position inside the low 24 bits, so no mask at the caller or in appendBase64Group can recover it; both declared compensating edits leave the trigger at Y2Fm/6k=. Restoring the & 0xFF in packGroup alone makes the trigger and the full suite pass.
trigger: com.fasterxml.jackson.core.base64.TestBase64Codec::testMimeOutputForUtf8Bytes is a new JUnit3 method in src/test/java/com/fasterxml/jackson/core/base64/TestBase64Codec.java. It builds byte[] { 'c', 'a', 'f', (byte) 0xC3, (byte) 0xA9 } (UTF-8 of 'caf' plus U+00E9) and asserts that Base64Variants.MIME.encode(input, false) equals "Y2Fmw6k=". It calls E directly. No new imports. The extra ownership test TestBase64Codec::testCharactersPerGroup is also new. It calls CharTypes.appendBase64Group(MIME, sb, 0xE29C93, 3) and (MIME, sb, 0xF00000, 1) and asserts "4pyT8A==". It adds the import com.fasterxml.jackson.core.io.CharTypes.
construction_notes:
Candidates considered first and rejected:
- CharTypes.appendQuoted: JsonStringEncoder.quoteAsString is an exact alternative implementation of the same escaping, which violates rule 5.
- VersionUtil.parseVersion: the existing protected parseVersionPart would remain as a sibling, and the computation is thin.
- NumberInput.parseAsInt: parseAsLong is a near-duplicate.
- Base64 line-wrap or padding faults inside the chain: the existing TestBase64Generation::testStreamingWrites compares encode() with the independent generator encoders for four variants, so such faults would fail a second test.
The existing suite only passes ASCII text through Base64Variant.encode, so the sign-extension omission in packGroup is reached only by the new trigger.
Context edits, all behaviour-preserving:
- E's body becomes a single delegation.
- H1 reproduces the old loop exactly: a linefeed only after complete groups, counter reset to maxLineLength>>2, and no linefeed after the final partial group.
- H2 masks every byte. The old partial path left the first byte unmasked, but only bits 18 to 23 are consumed, so the output is identical.
- H3 dispatches to the unchanged encodeBase64Chunk / encodeBase64Partial.
Checks in a /private/tmp scratch copy:
- CORRECT configuration: full suite 208 tests, 0 failures; trigger and both ownership tests pass.
- Variant: only the trigger fails, byte-identical three times, with expected:<Y2Fm[w]6k=> but was:<Y2Fm[/]6k=>.
- Both compensating edits (mask with 0xFFFFFF in H1, and in H3's partial path) leave the trigger failing with the same message.
The validator ran once and gave overall READY with every gate passing (G0 to G13; G6 saw the gold and all 3 decoys; baseline failures: none). mx_package_new.py packaged the instance as CTV-E04F64. Scratch directories were deleted, and the fresh checkout was not modified.
concerns: 1) A missing & 0xFF in a byte-packing loop is a well-known Java sign-extension pattern, so the gold has noticeable local oddness. Models will probably locate packGroup quickly, which means the instance mainly tests whether E is ranked above the identified deep helper, and it may sit at ceiling. 2) The generators (UTF8JsonGenerator / WriterBasedJsonGenerator._writeBinary) still contain their own correct inline triplet packing with & 0xFF. They are protected instance methods that write to an output buffer, so E or H1 cannot be rerouted to them. Still, an auditor could note that a correct inline copy of the packing exists; inlining it into encodeToText would be a multi-line repair. 3) E's upstream javadoc and H1's summary sentence describe end-to-end base64 output, which is wrong on the trigger. Both satisfy their docs only compositionally (given packGroup's postcondition). H1's @return was written as 'Text built as described above' to keep its contract about its own composition. 4) H3's javadoc links to ByteArrayBuilder#packGroup as the producer of the group layout, and the new ownership test pins H3 on values with bit 23 set. Ownership is decided by the documentation as the recipe requires, but this makes the gold easier to reach. 5) No test pins H1 on non-ASCII input other than the trigger; H1's composition is pinned by testStreamingWrites on ASCII only. 6) The fault shows only when a byte of 0x80 or more is in the second or third position of a group: a high first byte alone sign-extends only above bit 23, which the 6-bit masks discard. A model may notice that some high bytes encode correctly; this is consistent with the gold. 7) Placement plausibility: packGroup is a static helper in ByteArrayBuilder, which otherwise has instance methods. It is documented as the reading counterpart of appendThreeBytes. appendBase64Group adds a core import to CharTypes (io already depends on core elsewhere). H1 is in Base64Variants, the same package as E. 8) Only two compensating edits are declared, the masks in H1 and H3. Neither can absorb the fault, because the sign extension of byte 2 overwrites byte 1 inside the low 24 bits.
